summary: We’re kicking off with a fun‑focused, low‑jargon approach that leans on proven formats like quick‑demo carousels and relatable before/after reels—these have driven high engagement for similar creators even without past data for us. By surfacing bite‑sized wins (e.g., “Turn a boring email into a meme in 3 clicks”) and myth‑busting bits, we’ll tap the audience’s curiosity while keeping the vibe light and encouraging.
notes: Hook ideas: • “Claude Opus 5.5 just learned to write jokes—see it in action in 15 seconds!” (use a quick screen‑record of a simple prompt). • “GPT‑6 Sol & Luna sound like space rockets, but they’re actually free AI photo editors—here’s how to make your selfie pop.” • “Myth: AI will replace your brain. Reality: It can help you write a grocery list in under a minute—watch the before/after.” Visual style: bright pastel palettes, bold handwritten‑style fonts, playful emojis, and simple step‑by‑step graphics. Captions: start with a question or surprise fact, keep sentences <20 words, add a CTA like “Try it today and tag us!” Use trending headlines as hook frames but translate them into everyday scenarios (e.g., “What if your phone could ‘gzip’ a whole paragraph? It can—here’s the cheat sheet”). Post schedule: 3 carousels (tool demo, 3‑step tutorial, myth bust) and 2 single‑image quotes (fun AI fact, relatable fail) spread across the week to maintain momentum.
